title: Liberal justice system slammed after repeat sex offender is released
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — An Ontario Conservative MP blasted years of the lax approach to crime the Liberal government has taken after police warned about the release into the general public of a high-risk sex offender and pedophile. “Our children’s safety is NOT negotiable,” Ontario Conservative MP Rhonda Kirkland said in an X post. … However, the current federal Liberal government under Prime Minister Mark Carney has been soft on those charged with child pornography. Indeed, a recent Supreme Court ruling found that a mandatory one-year sentence for possessing or accessing child pornography is “unconstitutional.” The ruling was blasted by both Conservative and non-Conservative politicians, with Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew saying that anyone caught with child pornography should be “buried under the prison.” Despite the outrage from left and right provincial leaders, the Canadian federal government under Carney said it would not be looking to overturn the ruling.

title: Alberta holds historic vote today on whether to leave Canada
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — Canadians in the province of Alberta are taking part in a historic vote today, which allows people to decide whether or not the province should, in the future, hold a referendum to separate from Canada. Elections Alberta estimates turnout is extremely high, beating the last general election turnout. Current Premier of Alberta Danielle Smith, while allowing the vote due to many in her United Conservative Party (UCP) wanting independence, has urged people to vote to stay in Canada. … Recently, as reported by LifeSiteNews, Elon Musk weighed in on the debate around some Canadian provinces potentially becoming independent, saying that Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Quebec should leave Canada. Calls for Alberta’s independence have grown since Liberal Prime Minister Mark Carney defeated Poilievre in the 2025 federal election. In Alberta, all but two seats went to the Conservatives. Carney, like former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau before him, said that he is opposed to new pipeline projects that would allow Alberta oil and gas to be extracted, although he appears to be softening his stance due to high oil prices as a result of the U.S.-Iran war.
